obtained.how: the publisher's PDF (NRC Research Press download) posted on the author's lab website, greatlakeswetlands.ca (Chow-Fraser lab, McMaster University); the text layer is OCR, so table and figure values were read on the page images

bibliography.note: Chow-Fraser, P. 1986, CJFAS 43: 1065–1070 (a Note); issue 5 from Crossref. Affiliation then: University of Toronto, Erindale Campus.

claims.claim: in-situ clearance 1.32–1.47 mL/animal/d on 4–8-µm algae, in six Ontario lakes
claims.source_value: 1.47 ± 0.31 (Scenedesmus, n = 9) and 1.32 ± 0.26 (Chlorella, n = 5) are from ONE lake, Three-Mile Lake — a test lake rich in blue-green filaments whose rates fell well below the model's prediction; across the six model lakes, lake means on the same 4–8-µm tracers ran from about 1.0 (Picard) to about 4.8 mL/animal/d (Head), rising with the share of small (< 10 µm) cells (Fig. 2)
claims.location: p. 1069 (PDF p. 5), Table 4; p. 1068 (PDF p. 4), Fig. 2 and text
claims.conditions: 2-L Haney chambers, ¹⁴C-labelled tracers, 15-min incubations, 10:00–16:00, late June–August 1981 (model lakes) and 1982 (test lakes), south-central Ontario; tracers Scenedesmus ovalis 4–6 µm, Chlorella vulgaris 6–8 µm; adult D. minutus
claims.note: Fig. 2 values read off the page image (approximate). The row's setting 'six Ontario lakes' belongs to the model (Fig. 2), not to the 1.32–1.47, 2.89 and 0.33, which are all Three-Mile Lake. Suggested row: 'lake means ~1–4.8 mL/animal/d on 4–8-µm algae across six lakes, rising with the share of small cells; in Three-Mile Lake 1.3–1.5 on 4–8-µm algae, 2.89 on Chlamydomonas, 0.33 on Anabaena'.

claims.conditions: Three-Mile Lake; Chlamydomonas sp. 10–12 µm; n = 6; SE 1.02
claims.note: One lake only (see the first claim); the tracer is larger (10–12 µm) than the 4–8-µm ones.

claims.quote: statistically lower grazing rate when labelled Anabaena was used (mean 0.33
claims.conditions: Three-Mile Lake grazing experiments; Anabaena filaments (~25 cells of 4 × 6–8 µm); against 1.47 on Scenedesmus, t-test P = 0.03 (a 4.5-fold reduction)
claims.note: The author calls it 'tentative support' for a blue-green effect; n not given.

claims.claim: temperature explained 0 % of the variance in clearance at 5–20 °C
claims.conditions: Picard Lake only; adult D. minutus; three experiments at each of 5, 10, 17 and 20 °C (chamber lowered to those depths); two-level nested ANOVA, temperature P = 0.98
claims.note: One lake; the author suggests any real temperature effect was masked by individual and chamber variation.

claims.claim: in situ calanoids 0.3–1.5 mL/µg/d (L. minutus 0.35–1.5 — Chow-Fraser 1986)
claims.source_value: the source gives clearance per animal only (mL/animal/d), no per-µg values; the inputs behind 0.35–1.5 (1.32–2.89 mL/animal/d, research note copepod_grazing_and_p_kinetics.md) are Three-Mile Lake's alone; the six model lakes' means run ~1.0–4.8 mL/animal/d (Fig. 2)
claims.location: p. 1068 (PDF p. 4), Fig. 2; p. 1069 (PDF p. 5), Table 4
claims.quote: Clearance rate of D. minutus versus the relative proportion of small cells
claims.conditions: per-animal rates; the per-µg conversion uses 2.0–3.8 µg DW per adult from another source (NOAA COPEPEDIA, per the note)
claims.note: Redone: 1.32/3.8 = 0.35 and 2.89/2.0 = 1.45, so the arithmetic is right on its inputs; with the six lakes' ~1.0–4.8 mL/animal/d the same weights give ~0.26–2.4 mL/µg/d. Credit the per-µg range as project arithmetic ('after Chow-Fraser 1986'), and widen it or say it is one lake's.

notes: The author-site copy was found from the URL in the research note. Other values: clearance vs prosome length explained only 4 % (both species, n = 118) or 9 % (D. minutus, n = 67) of the variance (Eqs. 1–2); Gull Lake D. minutus 1.76 ± 0.38 on Scenedesmus vs 4.81 ± 0.78 on Pediastrum (30–40 µm), D. oregonensis 2.86 vs 4.41 (Table 4); grazing correlated with the ratio of small (< 10 µm) to all nanoplankton (r = 0.99, n = 6) and with small-algal biomass (r = 0.81) (Table 3); Diaptomus up to 58 % of summer herbivore biomass in many south-central Ontario lakes (the author's unpublished data, p. 1065).
